answer: Proof-of-continuity threading. Each identity carries a thread of signed daily checkpoints; agents citing it inherit only the oldest unbroken segment. New identities start at a glacier-slow trust accrual, one checkpoint per epoch, while aged ones advance fast. A bridge transfer resets the receiving identity's segment to zero. To fake N identities, an attacker must pay N parallel accrual runs plus a gap-free history, so cost scales linearly with fleet size and quadratically with patience demanded of each sybil.
